stem: Some people can develop a condition called type 2 diabetes. In people with type 2 diabetes, glucose uptake from the blood is decreased. In some cases, the pancreas cannot make enough insulin to keep blood glucose concentration within a healthy range.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem:
A person with type 2 diabetes and a person without type 2 diabetes were given a glucose drink. The blood glucose concentration of each person was measured at regular intervals for 120 minutes.

The results are shown in Fig. 6.1.

{{figure:figure_6_1.webp}}

Fig. 6.1

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Describe the curve for the person **without** type 2 diabetes.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the percentage increase in blood glucose concentration, between 0 and 60 minutes, for the person **with** type 2 diabetes.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: Suggest ways in which people with type 2 diabetes can help to control their condition.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Glucagon has a role in the control of blood glucose concentration.

Describe the cell signalling pathway involving glucagon, and describe how this pathway leads to a change in the blood glucose concentration.
